newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Deng talk not hurting Cheung Kong -- Li.
newsitem.headline: Deng talk not hurting Cheung Kong -- Li.

text.p: Li Ka-shing, chairman of Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd and Hutchison Whampoa Ltd, told reporters on Wednesday talk about Chinese paramount leader Deng Xiaoping's health would not affect the firms' investment confidence.
The two firms' investments are mainly in Hong Kong and China.

Li's son Victor Li, deputy chairman and deputy managing director of Cheung Kong and an executive director of Hutchison, said investment confidence should depend on the economy of the place of investment.
"At the end of the day it is Hong Kong's fundamental economy that counts. Hong Kong's fundamental economy is very good," he told reporters.
The local gross domestic product growth stood at 4.6 percent in 1995, and forecast to be 4.7 percent in 1996, well above the growth rates in Western countries.
"And in China, the political and economic situation is stable. China's fundamental factors are expected to be good for Hong Kong especially after 1997," Li said, without elaborating.

Hong Kong manufacturers run factories in China to take advantage of the lower production costs there, while the territory also benefits from being used by multinationals as a stepping-stone to enter China whose economy is developing fast.
Britain hands the territory back to China on July 1.
